forecast-period.text: A trough of low pressure over central South Australia reaches southeastern parts later and lingers in the east, before weakening from Thursday. A slow moving high pressure system in the Tasman Sea re-establishes a ridge across southern parts from Wednesday. Another series of troughs move into western parts on Thursday and broadly across SA on Friday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and thunderstorms in the east and northwest. Thunderstorms possibly severe with heavy rainfall which may lead to flash flooding possible about and to the south of the Mid North and Riverland. Severe storms that may develop over the Flinders Ranges have additional risks of damaging wind gusts and large hail. Maximum temperatures above average. South to southeasterly winds in the west, tending northeast to northwesterly over eastern districts, ahead of a southerly change slowly clearing east during the day.
Showers and possible thunderstorms about central and southeastern districts. North to northeasterly winds, shifting northwesterly ahead of a southerly change moving across the state.

Showers and possible thunderstorms in the northwest and east, clearing from the southeast during the evening. Maximum temperatures above average. Southeast to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes. Winds tending southwesterly in the far northeast during the day.

Areas of morning fog in the south. Showers and possible thunderstorms in the north. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average near the coasts. East to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes. Winds tending north to northwesterly ahead of a south to southeasterly change moving into the west during the evening.

text.p: Showers and possible thunderstorms in the north, developing about central and southeastern parts later. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average in the south. Southeast to northeasterly winds, tending northeast to northwesterly ahead of a southwest to southerly change moving across from the west.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Friday: 2 to 10 mm broadly across SA, increasing to 10 to 20 mm about the far northwest and possibly about the Flinders Ranges and eastern districts. Isolated heavier falls between 20 to 40 mm are possible with thunderstorms extending south from the Flinders Ranges into the Mid North, Fleurieu Peninsula and into the east and southeast.
